```{r}
#| label: create-functions

run_replication <- function(replication, model) {
  set.seed(410000L + replication)
  population <- create_baseline_population(params$initial_population, 60, 2000, 
    group_weights = c("A" = 1, "B" = 1, "C" = 1))
  model <- model |> set_population(population)
  time <- system.time(result <- simulate(model, params$years, 420000L + replication))[["elapsed"]]
  result$runtime <- time
  return(result)
}
```

## Overview of Design


## Inputs and Simulation Design

We will reproduce the demographic transition in Sweden! It has HMD and HFD data that go far enough back.

```{r}
fertility_rates_sweden <- get_fertility_hfd("SWE", 1891:2020)
mortality_rates_sweden <- get_mortality_hmd("SWE", 1800:2020, open_age = 95)
```

We only have fertility back to 1891, but we were along in terms of mortality decline then. So lets just take the 1891 fertility rates back to a year where we get a roughly stationary population. Then we will take use those rates for a 100 years to produce a stable population for the actual starting population of the simulation. Then run it forward.

Codex thinks 1810 would be a good starting year for mortality. Don't know if I need to go back that far. I can create a get_growth_rate() function that uses the log(NRR)/(mu) approximation to estimate growth rates for candidates quickly

```{r}

get_growth_rate <- function(fert_rates, mort_rates) {

  NRR <- mort_rates |> calculate_life_table() |>
    filter(sex == "f") |>
    select(age_start, Lx) |>
    right_join(fert_rates, by = c("age_start")) |>
    mutate(prod = Lx * rate) |>
    pull(prod) |>
    sum() * 0.4886
  mu <- sum((fert_rates$age_start + 0.5) * fert_rates$rate) / sum(fert_rates$rate)

  log(NRR)/mu

}


fert_rates <- fertility_rates_sweden |> filter(time_start == 1891)
get_growth_rate(fert_rates, mortality_rates_sweden |> filter(time_start == 1811))
get_growth_rate(fert_rates, mortality_rates_sweden |> filter(time_start == 1810))
get_growth_rate(fert_rates, mortality_rates_sweden |> filter(time_start == 1812))
get_growth_rate(fert_rates, mortality_rates_sweden |> filter(time_start == 1813))
get_growth_rate(fert_rates, mortality_rates_sweden |> filter(time_start == 1838))
```

It looks like 1811 is the winner.

```{r}

fert_rates <- fertility_rates_sweden |> filter(time_start == 1891) |>
  select(-starts_with("time_"))
mort_rates <- mortality_rates_sweden |> filter(time_start == 1811) |>
  select(-starts_with("time_"))

pop <- create_baseline_population(50000, 70, 1811 - 100)
model <- hammel_model() |>
  set_population(pop) |>
  set_fertility(fert_rates) |>
  set_mortality(mort_rates) |>
  set_union_formation("on_demand")
pop_start <- simulate(model, 100, 1)
```

```{r}
mort_rates_time <- mortality_rates_sweden |> filter(time_start >= 1770)
fert_rates_time <- fertility_rates_sweden |> 
  mutate(time_start = if_else(time_start == 1891, 1770, time_start))

model <- hammel_model() |>
  set_population(pop_start) |>
  set_fertility(fert_rates_time) |>
  set_mortality(mort_rates_time) |>
  set_union_formation("on_demand")
pop_final <- simulate(model, 2020 - 1811, 1)

```

```{r}
pop_final |> calculate_population_size(1770:2020) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = time, y = population))+
  geom_line()

```

```{r}
# get crude rates
cbr_f <- calculate_fertility_rates(pop_final, 1770:2020, c(0, Inf)) |> 
  mutate(rate_fertility = rate_fertility * 0.4886) |>
  select(time_start, rate_fertility)
cmr_f <- calculate_mortality_rates(pop_final, 1770:2020, c(0, Inf)) |> 
  filter(sex == "f") |>
  select(time_start, rate_mortality)
full_join(cbr_f, cmr_f) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("rate_"), names_prefix = "rate_",
               names_to = "type", values_to = "crude_rate") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = time_start, y = crude_rate, color = type))+
  geom_line()

```
